issues.explanation: 'Avoid Exercise' is not clinically coherent with the rest of the profile. The threat items center on hypervigilance about nighttime intrusion and safety checking in the home, while the memory and appraisal items focus on intrusive assault memories, danger, and physical vulnerability. Exercise avoidance addresses a different symptom domain and lacks plausible linkage to the selected threat, memory, or appraisal content. In contrast, magical thinking and mirror checking fit better with maladaptive attempts to manage threat and distress.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Physical Vulnerability: My body has been permanently damaged by what happened
issues.explanation: These two selected items are difficult to reconcile within the same profile. A strong appraisal of permanent bodily damage implies acknowledgment of serious ongoing physical consequences, whereas telling oneself the event did not really happen or was not that bad reflects minimization/denial of the trauma's reality or impact. While some ambivalence can occur clinically, this pair pulls in opposing directions strongly enough to question internal coherence in this profile.

vignette: Mrs. Amina Johnson is a 78-year-old African American widow who has been struggling with the aftermath of an assault that occurred several months ago. Since then, she has found herself navigating through a complex web of fears and maladaptive coping strategies that have gradually eroded her sense of security. On the night of the traumatic event, Amina was in her home studio, working on a new batch of pottery late into the evening. She heard a noise from outside and went to check it out, only to find herself confronted by an intruder who forcibly entered her home. The assault left her shaken and deeply afraid. Since that night, specific triggers have haunted her daily life, making her feel perpetually on edge. The memory of the assault forces its way into Amina’s mind at unexpected moments, often triggered by sounds or images reminiscent of that terrifying evening. She relives the event vividly, feeling as if she is right back in her studio with the intruder looming over her. This uncontrolled access to traumatic memories has led Amina to believe that thinking about the event will overwhelm her and that she won't be able to handle it. Consequently, she tries hard not to think about what happened, engaging in thought suppression as a way to cope. Amina’s negative appraisals of the world have deepened her sense of danger, reinforcing her belief that the world is indeed a perilous place. This conviction has led her to develop several maladaptive strategies to manage her fears. She frequently checks mirrors around her home and repeatedly verifies that all locks and windows are secure. Her constant vigilance and the intrusive memories fuel each other in a vicious cycle: as she relives the assault, her fear intensifies, driving her to check locks and mirrors even more obsessively. The memory of the intruder’s presence has also shaped Amina's perception of safety. She is unable to relax even when she knows she is in a secure environment. Her body continues to react with intense anxiety as if danger still lurks around every corner. This heightened arousal further exacerbates her waking alertness, where she frequently wakes up during the night to ensure she is safe. The trauma has significantly impacted Amina’s daily life and work. As a potter, her studio is both a sanctuary and a trigger zone. The sounds of tools clinking or the flicker of her kiln can evoke vivid memories that send her into a state of panic. This fear has caused her to avoid working in her studio altogether for stretches at a time, leading to a noticeable decline in her productivity and a sense of loss about her craft. Amina’s efforts to suppress thoughts about the assault have only served to reinforce her negative appraisals. She is certain that the world remains dangerous, and these beliefs keep her trapped in a cycle where she constantly checks for threats and relives the event involuntarily. This reinforcing loop has grown stronger over time, making it increasingly difficult for Amina to find any semblance of peace or normalcy. It was not until her daughter noticed her growing withdrawal from social activities and her increasing anxiety that Amina finally sought help. She is most afraid that she will never feel safe again and that the memory of the assault will continue to dominate her life. Despite these fears, she hopes to regain control over her thoughts and daily routines and find a way to once again enjoy the peace and creativity of her pottery work.
